fit: review grouping two standalone preparations and one adjunctive trial
assessment: Table 2 lists three distinct lemon-balm trial families. Araj-Khodaei used dried leaf powder and an active comparator. The 45 analyzed participants show no clearly distinguishable difference between treatments in Hamilton Depression Rating Scale change, with no equivalence test or placebo. Safari compared a dried aerial-part extract with placebo in type 2 diabetes. The reported Beck Depression Inventory change favored the extract among the 44 participants who completed follow-up. Solberg included a combination arm, confirmed in the original article despite the egg-focused title. With the egg preparation matched, adding Melissa to it did not produce a clearly distinguishable depression difference. These three cohorts were already assessed. None compared brewed lemon-balm tea with a control in Parkinson disease.

fit: dried sage and time-dependent acute alertness during a laboratory stressor
assessment: In a crossover study of 30 healthy adults, 300 mg dried sage raised pre-stress alertness and was associated with a larger stress-task alertness decline at one and four hours. The higher dose had a different pre-stress pattern. Alertness under a laboratory task does not measure sustained fatigue, and drying and population limit transfer.
